subject.title: [Feature]: Mobile apps: per-gateway custom headers for gateways behind authenticating proxies

question: Should OpenClaw mobile apps support arbitrary per-gateway custom headers for authenticating proxies, or should the first native proxy-auth contract be narrower and typed?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this feature stores and replays pre-Gateway credentials from native apps, so owner/security intent is needed before accepting arbitrary operator-supplied headers as the permanent product surface.

options.title: Adopt shared custom-header contract
options.body: Proceed with the iOS and Android PRs after owner/security review confirms secure storage, reserved-header filtering, redaction, gateway-only attachment, and real authenticated-proxy proof.

options.title: Narrow to typed proxy auth
options.body: Ask the platform PRs to expose only approved Basic, Bearer, or fixed service-token fields first, reducing arbitrary-header risk at the cost of less operator flexibility.

options.title: Defer native proxy credentials
options.body: Keep mobile proxy credential injection unsupported for now and document VPN, Tailscale, or proxy-bypass alternatives while the broader design remains unsettled.

recommendation.title: Adopt shared custom-header contract
recommendation.body: Proceed with the iOS and Android PRs after owner/security review confirms secure storage, reserved-header filtering, redaction, gateway-only attachment, and real authenticated-proxy proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the issue and linked PRs and has the strongest current signal across the mobile gateway and security/product boundary.
